title: Still think about this all the time! 😬 #storytime #theatre
transcript: One time someone tried to spread her husband's ashes on the stage after a play and I witnessed this interaction with my own two eyes the year was 2019 and I was volunteer ushering a show at the Lucille Lortell Theater and the show was Mac Beth which as a quick side note is a fascinating reimagining of Mac Beth death loosely inspired by the Slender Man stabbing the concept is that like a group of girls gather in an empty lot to act out the play Macbeth but things end up getting a little too real. Also my childhood crush on a Sophia Rob was in the play and that was its own hilarious interaction but anyway, the reason I mentioned the show is that the the stage was covered in fake grass and I guess because people spread ashes in nature a lot of the time that made it less obvious to this woman that what she was doing was weird so the show is over and the audience has mostly cleared out except for this one woman who approaches the edge of the stage so my friend who I was ushering with goes up to her and is like, uh, hey, can I help you? She said I would like to spread my husband's ashes on this stage because The Lucia Lortel Theatre was very important to my husband I don't remember my friend's exact response but it was something to the effect of like, no, you Definitely can't do that. And I don't mean to laugh at this woman who was surely not having a good time and this incident definitely didn't help. But at the same time, you had to know that this was deeply inappropriate, probably unsafe and also kind of stupid because like what you thought just cause the stage looks like grass, that they don't clean it regularly, that it's just gonna stay there not only through the end of the run, but forever after as your husband's final resting place. Like, no, his ashes would have ended up in a vacuum cleaner and then the trash. So yeah, that was definitely one of the craziest things I've ever seen as a volunteer usher.
